reviewed_by: Claude review of per-conversation record lookups
reason: ChatService.pending_turn, ChatGoalService.get, ChatScheduleService.get and ToolOutputService._call_artifacts each read the first 1,000-row page of a whole entity kind (list_entities orders oldest first) and filtered by session or tool call in Python. Once Core holds more than 1,000 chat turns in total, pending_turn stops seeing any newer conversation's active turn, so the guards on sending, editing in place, scheduling and subagent delivery silently stop working; past 1,000 goals or schedules a newer conversation's goal or schedule is reported missing (GET 404, POST creates a duplicate, schedules skip with 'No conversation goal'); past ~1,000 artifacts in a project tool_output.search returns no matches for newer calls. NebulaStore.list_session_entities and list_tool_call_artifacts now filter on the JSON payload in SQL, and _persist_turn_inputs uses the same query. test_session_record_lookups pins each lookup beyond the first thousand rows; the goal, schedule, storage and specialist-batch suites cover the callers (the specialist loop reads tool output through _call_artifacts).
exclusions: No frontend tests: no ui/ change. No native tests: no Tauri or Rust change. No Playwright: area:core-api (matched through storage.py) is the real-Core journey suite; no HTTP contract or rendered state changes, and the defect only appears past 1,000 rows, which the Python tests build directly. No full suites.
